objectives: Recognize recurring -an and -ap sound-spelling patterns in taught CVC words.
Compare words that share an ending while attending to the changing initial consonant.
Apply word-family knowledge without replacing full grapheme-by-grapheme decoding.
concepts: Word families contain recurring rime patterns such as -an and -ap.
The initial consonant can change while the shared ending remains stable.
Pattern recognition supports automaticity but does not replace decoding.

definitions.definition: A group of words sharing a common ending sound-spelling pattern.
The vowel and following sounds in a syllable, such as -an or -ap.
Reading text restricted mainly to taught sound-spelling patterns.

workedExamples: man and pan share -an but differ in the initial consonant.
map and nap share -ap but differ in the initial consonant.
Read the full word even when the ending is familiar.
commonMistakes: Reading a familiar pattern without checking every grapheme.
keyTakeaways: Use patterns to support, not replace, decoding.
revisionPoints: Shared ending + changing onset = word family pattern.

basic: Sort taught words into -an and -ap families.
conceptual: Identify which part stays the same and which changes.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why word families should not encourage guessing.
mixedReview: Sort, decode, read and answer controlled-text questions.

mistakeBasedRevision: If the family is recognized but the word is wrong, return to full decoding.
weakTopicRevision: Read each word sound by sound, then reread the family for automaticity.

outcomes: Learner sorts taught words into -an and -ap families with at least 80% accuracy.
Learner identifies the shared ending and changing initial consonant.
Learner reads word-family words accurately without guessing.
Learner answers simple controlled-text questions with at least 80% accuracy.
